newsitem.title: USA: Ball sees Q3 below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Ball sees Q3 below expectations.

text.p: Ball Corp, which makes metal and plastic packaging, said Monday its third quarter results from continuing operations likely will not exceed year-ago results, as it had previously expected.
"While we had expected results from continuing operations to exceed last year's third quarter, it now appears that will not be the case," George Sissel, chairman, said in a statement.
In the third quarter of 1995, Ball earned $0.62 a share before charges related to the sale of its glass business.

Ball said third quarter results for this year would not meet earlier expectations, due largely to lower than anticipated beverage cans shipments, the negative effects of declines in aluminum prices, and lower food can shipments attributable to a later than forecast food pack.

"In addition to the pressures on our North American can businesses, somewhat higher costs associated with startups in our new PET plastic container business and with our new international can manufacturing joint ventures are having a negative impact on our third quarter," Sissel said.
He said the company continues to make "consistent progress" in implementing its growth strategies.
He cited plans to sell its 42 percent interest in Ball-Foster Glass Container LLC to Compagnie de Saint-Gobain for about $190 million, which was announced earlier Monday.
Ball also opened three new can plants in China in recent months, has beverage can and end plants under construction in Brazil and Thailand, and us building a fourth PET container plant in Ames, Iowa.
